webpage_capture_policy: For a readable webpage, the default development path is interactive read -> faithful claim-scoped visible-text capture plus source/provenance metadata -> bounded local database capture capsule -> Google Drive handoff. Do not invoke GitHub Actions merely to fetch or archive webpage HTML. The local database is a capture/handoff envelope, not live PostgreSQL authority and not automatic Fact/Judgment publication. Preserve original URL, publisher/source identity, title/date when supported, capture timestamp, capture_mode, visible text, text SHA-256 and any material limitation.

pdf_source_policy.locator_verified: Publisher/document identity and PDF locator are verified. Record original URL, publisher/source identity, title/date when supported, filename when known, verification time/mode and materialization_status. Locator existence alone is not sufficient to prove a claim whose content was not read.
pdf_source_policy.content_verified: The Agent has actually read claim-relevant PDF content in a trustworthy interactive surface and can preserve a claim-scoped excerpt/page/section or equivalent readable grounding. This is sufficient to enter normal Evidence semantics even if raw PDF bytes have not yet been downloaded or hashed. Record capture/read mode and any representation limitation truthfully.
pdf_source_policy.materialized: A later normal-network Agent has downloaded the recorded PDF locator, verified document identity/content, and added raw byte size, SHA-256 and a durable storage locator. Materialization is completeness/integrity enrichment, not a prerequisite for already content-verified claim grounding.
pdf_source_policy.mainstream_source_rule: PDFs on mainstream official/regulatory/issuer/institutional publisher sites are accepted as legitimate source documents once publisher/document identity and locator are verified. Do not spend research time proving that GitHub Actions or the current Agent can download the bytes. Claim-scoped authority still comes from publisher/document role and scope; transport or the .pdf suffix never upgrades authority.
pdf_source_policy.deferred_agent_instruction: When a later Agent has normal network access, download pending_materialization PDFs from their recorded URLs, verify the document identity and previously grounded content, then append size/SHA/storage metadata. If materialized bytes contradict the earlier verified content or identity, fail closed and open an integrity repair instead of silently replacing the earlier record.

github_actions_pdf_policy: Do not create or run GitHub Actions merely to download new PDF source bytes. Actions may still be used for PostgreSQL/runtime execution. Historical one-shot PDF acquisition workflows and immutable Release packs are legacy development artifacts and remain valid under their existing receipts, but they are not the default path for new PDFs.
github_release_policy: Existing immutable GitHub Release PDF/source packs remain valid historical materializations and may be reused when already available. Do not require a new Release asset before proceeding with content-verified PDF Evidence. New deferred raw-byte materialization may use an appropriate normal-network Agent and durable object/file transport chosen by the owning receipt; Release is no longer mandatory.
google_drive_policy: Google Drive is the development handoff relay for bounded local webpage-capture databases and Longcycle-generated binary state: DuckDB/SQLite webpage capture capsules, replay materializations, execution/reconciliation outputs, generated database snapshots and offline runtimes. Continue the proven private authorized-Drive path: checkpoint/close and hash the local database, upload a new object to google_drive_folder_id, capture exact file id/name/MIME/size/SHA, download it back by id, verify the outer bytes and open/read it locally, then record the receipt in Git. Do not move large generated database bytes to GitHub merely because work is parallel. A webpage capture capsule contains source-derived visible text and provenance, so Drive transport does not turn that text into a generated research conclusion or change source authority. Deferred raw PDF materialization is optional and governed by its owning receipt rather than required by this handoff manifest. Drive is not live transactional database authority.
postgres_policy: Do not transport a live PostgreSQL cluster as session state or place it in GitHub Release. PostgreSQL remains the transactional write/ops engine and is rebuilt in a service-capable runtime when writes, leases or outbox semantics are required. Parallel workers use isolated databases or schemas derived from their fenced workstream identity and never share a writable development schema. Canonical migration allocation and integration remain serial. If a generated database snapshot is ever needed for handoff, it belongs in Google Drive and remains an immutable snapshot rather than live authority.
duckdb_policy: DuckDB is the preferred bounded local container for webpage visible-text capture capsules and portable read/replay state; SQLite is an acceptable bounded capture envelope when DuckDB is not available in the current interactive runtime. Before handoff, checkpoint/close the capsule, record SHA-256/size/schema/source count, upload a new immutable capsule to Google Drive, and verify the downloaded bytes. After restore, research/replay capsules open read-only by default; a worker that must transform one first copies it into private workstream storage and emits a new candidate rather than modifying the restored base.
parallel_database_policy: A worker downloads only an exact main-promoted database generation pinned by lane id, generation id, Drive file id and optional Drive revision, SHA-256, byte size and schema revision. It verifies those facts before opening the file, restores into private workstream storage and treats the base as read-only. Worker writes use an isolated PostgreSQL database/schema or a copied DuckDB/SQLite file. Workers may upload immutable candidates or deterministic change bundles, but may never overwrite a Drive object, mutate a shared database, or edit the global generation head; only the single serial integration lane may promote a generation.
drive_generation_policy: Google Drive is immutable object transport, not the current-version authority. Exact file identity/revision plus SHA-256 and size identify bytes; names and folder listing order never do. The refreshed main data-plane manifest carries at most eight active generation heads. Before promotion, the serial integration lane compares the candidate base generation with the current head, replays compatible candidates sequentially in an isolated integration database, resolves schema and semantic conflicts, verifies the result, uploads a new immutable object, round-trip verifies it, and updates the Git head only when the expected predecessor is still current. A stale candidate is replayed or rejected, never promoted by last-writer-wins.
drive_upload_recovery_policy: Before the proven authorized ChatGPT/Drive upload, push a bounded intent receipt with a stable operation key, unique candidate name, workstream and assignment fence, producer head, base generation, expected digest/size and google_drive_folder_id. Upload a new private object; never replace the base. Capture its file/revision identity, download it back by id, verify and open/read the database, then push an outcome receipt with observed digest/size and download_back_verified. If interruption leaves intent without outcome, inspect the exact folder/name and verify any match by digest before retrying; ambiguous external state is BLOCKED and blind re-upload is forbidden. Candidate history remains behind exact receipts while this manifest keeps only active promoted heads.
legacy_release_web_policy: Previously produced immutable Release assets that include webpage/HTML bytes are grandfathered. Never mutate or silently relocate them. All new readable webpage captures follow local database -> Google Drive unless a future explicit architecture decision supersedes this policy.
historical_asset_index_policy: This manifest is resume-relevant, not an exhaustive historical asset inventory. Assets no longer required by the live continuation cursor may be pruned from this file without deleting or invalidating them; durable research/execution receipts plus Git history retain their exact identities and restore metadata. Database generation heads contain only the bounded active promoted pointers; predecessor and candidate history stays behind integration receipts. Re-enter an old workstream through its durable receipt rather than keeping every historical binary in fresh-Agent context.
missing_required_asset_action: Missing raw PDF bytes are not an integrity blocker when the claim-relevant PDF content has already been content_verified and the locator/provenance are preserved. Fail closed only when the claim depends on PDF content that was not actually read, when a required webpage/generated capsule is missing or corrupt, or when later PDF materialization contradicts the verified source identity/content.
supersession_policy: Never silently replace a verified source identity, captured visible text, materialized byte object or generated capsule. A later PDF materialization enriches the same source locator with byte metadata only after identity/content verification; contradictory bytes create an integrity repair. Successor webpage/generated capsules get new Drive identities.
